title: One-hot EX forwarding to shorten the critical path
motivation: The baseline's worst path runs from the MEM/WB destination register through the forwarding unit and EX ALU to the memory address output, with 156 logic cells and 199.837 ns arrival time. The current two-bit priority select is decoded again by a three-way operand mux on this path.

hypothesis.motivation: The baseline's worst path runs from the MEM/WB destination register through the forwarding unit and EX ALU to the memory address output, with 156 logic cells and 199.837 ns arrival time. The current two-bit priority select is decoded again by a three-way operand mux on this path.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Replace the two-bit forwarding selects with mutually exclusive one-hot selects for the register-file value, EX/MEM result, and MEM/WB result. Apply these selects as bit masks and an OR in EX, allowing the FPGA LUT mapping to combine forwarding selection with the operand path and reduce the comparator-to-ALU delay while preserving EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB priority.

lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-001-r1s0 (regression, +2.97%): Replacing EX forwarding muxes with three 32-bit one-hot AND/OR networks regressed, showing that replicated data gating can outweigh saved select decoding; check the mapped path before adopting this form.

title: Predecode forwarding selections
motivation: The baseline critical path starts at a MEM/WB destination register and crosses forwarding selection and the EX ALU before reaching the data-memory output. Register-destination equality checks are currently performed in EX, serializing compare, operand mux, and address arithmetic in one cycle.

hypothesis.motivation: The baseline critical path starts at a MEM/WB destination register and crosses forwarding selection and the EX ALU before reaching the data-memory output. Register-destination equality checks are currently performed in EX, serializing compare, operand mux, and address arithmetic in one cycle.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Compute each incoming instruction's forwarding source while it is in ID, using the current ID/EX and EX/MEM producers, then register the two select codes alongside the ID/EX operands. In EX, use those registered selectors to choose the EX/MEM or MEM/WB bypass value. This moves register-tag comparisons off the forwarding-mux-to-ALU path while preserving the existing one-cycle load-use interlock and producer priority.

title: Predict conditional branches with a small BHT
motivation: Conditional branches currently resolve in EX, so every taken branch redirects fetch after wrong-path instructions have entered the pipeline. CoreMark contains tight loops where backward branches are commonly taken, making branch direction prediction a plausible way to improve iterations per cycle.

hypothesis.motivation: Conditional branches currently resolve in EX, so every taken branch redirects fetch after wrong-path instructions have entered the pipeline. CoreMark contains tight loops where backward branches are commonly taken, making branch direction prediction a plausible way to improve iterations per cycle.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a 16-entry table of 2-bit saturating direction counters indexed by the branch PC, reset to weakly not taken. In IF, predict conditional branches from the table and form a taken target directly from the fetched branch immediate. Carry the predicted next PC with the instruction, train the counter when the branch resolves in EX, and redirect/flush only on a mismatch. This should remove most taken-loop branch bubbles with modest state and without a target cache.
